h1: Suicide Prevention Training Quiz & Practice Questions
subhead: Take a free practice quiz or get instant, explained answers to Suicide Prevention (Ask, Care, Escort) questions — recognizing warning signs and intervening the right way, without the guesswork.
metaTitle: Suicide Prevention Training Quiz & Practice Questions | Cambo
metaDescription: Free Suicide Prevention (ACE) quiz and practice questions with instant, explained answers. Warning signs, the Ask-Care-Escort model, and how to intervene.
whyItWorks: ACE scenarios test whether you take the direct, active step the model actually calls for — asking plainly, staying with the person, escorting them to help — instead of a softer, well-meaning response that leaves them alone. Cambo explains why the direct option is correct, not just which one it is.

sampleQuestions.q: What does the acronym ACE stand for in DoD suicide prevention training?
options: Assess, Contact, Evaluate
Ask, Care, Escort
Alert, Counsel, Engage
Assist, Coordinate, Elevate
sampleQuestions.a: ACE stands for Ask, Care, Escort — a three-step model for recognizing warning signs and directly intervening with someone who may be at risk of suicide.

sampleQuestions.q: A coworker mentions offhand that they feel like giving up and don't see the point anymore. According to the ACE model, what's the first step?
options: Wait a few days to see if they bring it up again
Report the comment to their supervisor without speaking to them directly
Ask them directly and calmly whether they are thinking about suicide
Change the subject to avoid making the moment more uncomfortable
sampleQuestions.a: Ask them directly and calmly whether they're thinking about suicide — the first step in ACE is asking the question plainly rather than dancing around it or waiting to see if it comes up again.

sampleQuestions.q: Why does ACE training specifically emphasize asking the direct question, using the word "suicide" rather than a softer phrase?
options: Because using the word is a legal reporting requirement
Because asking directly does not increase risk, and can open the door for the person to talk honestly instead of feeling like their pain has to stay hidden
Because indirect questions take longer to ask
Because only medical professionals are permitted to ask indirect questions
sampleQuestions.a: Asking directly does not increase risk — research behind the ACE model shows a direct question can actually come as a relief, opening the door for the person to talk honestly instead of guessing at what you mean.

sampleQuestions.q: After a coworker admits they've been thinking about suicide, what does the "Escort" step of ACE require?
options: Give them space and check back in the next day
Never leave the at-risk person alone — escort them to a chaplain, behavioral health provider, primary care, or emergency care
Ask a mutual friend to check on them later instead
Refer them to a phone hotline and consider your responsibility fulfilled
sampleQuestions.a: Never leave the person alone — the "Escort" step means physically staying with them and getting them to a chaplain, behavioral health provider, or emergency care, not just pointing them toward a resource and stepping away.

sampleQuestions.q: Which of the following is a recognized warning sign covered in suicide prevention training?
options: Giving away prized possessions or making final arrangements
Taking on additional responsibilities at work
Scheduling routine leave in advance
Expressing enthusiasm about an upcoming promotion
sampleQuestions.a: Giving away prized possessions, making final arrangements, or a sudden sense of calm after a period of visible depression are recognized warning signs — they can indicate the person has already made a decision, not that they're improving.

sampleQuestions.q: Under the ACE model, whose responsibility is it to intervene when a peer shows warning signs?
options: Only unit leadership and commanders
Only behavioral health professionals
Everyone — ACE is designed as a peer-level intervention skill, not something limited to leaders or clinicians
Only chaplains and medical personnel
sampleQuestions.a: Everyone — ACE is built around peer intervention, so any trained individual who notices warning signs is expected to act, not just leadership or behavioral health professionals.

faqs.q: How often is suicide prevention training required?
faqs.a: Annually, typically delivered as unit-level training — the exact regulation and cadence varies by service branch.

faqs.q: Who has to complete this training?
faqs.a: All service members; it's also made available to DoD civilian employees in most components, though specific requirements vary by branch.

faqs.q: What does the ACE acronym stand for?
faqs.a: Ask, Care, Escort — ask directly if someone is thinking about suicide, show you care by staying calm and listening without judgment, and escort them to help rather than leaving them alone.

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with the DoD or the Defense Suicide Prevention Office?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool, not produced or endorsed by the Department of Defense or the Defense Suicide Prevention Office.

faqs.q: How long does the training take?
faqs.a: It varies by service and audience — some versions run around 90 minutes for service members and closer to two hours for civilian employees, though exact timing depends on the specific course modules assigned.

faqs.q: Where can someone get help right now?
faqs.a: The Veterans/Military Crisis Line is available 24/7 — dial 988 and press 1, or text 838255. It's confidential and available to service members, veterans, and their families.
